x.hook: Looping Blend b-tokens shouldn't liquidate your stack across pools.
x.copy:
Looping Blend b-tokens shouldn't liquidate your stack across pools. Standard leverage exposes your positions to shared-pool bad debt whenever secondary tokens depeg.

Vanna routes credit through isolated SmartAccount sandboxes instead. Each position runs as an isolated Soroban contract instance, syncing state with ~320ms Mercury indexer latency and holding a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor.

linkedin.hook: Why shared pool lending models fail yield farmers on Soroban
linkedin.copy:
Blend v2 formally verified pools bring structural reliability to Stellar, but looping b-tokens on standard lending protocols still inherits systemic cross-collateral risks. When debt is pooled globally, a shortfall in an illiquid asset threatens solvent positions across the entire protocol. For allocators managing larger balances, sharing liquidation risk with arbitrary collateral types is an inefficient way to farm yield.

Vanna addresses this by running credit through isolated SmartAccount sandboxes. Rather than pooling user funds into a single contract balance sheet, each participant deploys a dedicated Soroban contract instance that interacts directly with Blend pools. With state verified through a ~320ms Mercury indexer latency pipeline and a hard-coded 1.10x Health Factor floor, position health is tracked independently. A liquidation inside one sandbox never bleeds into another.

Because Soroban execution costs sit at approximately 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per transaction, automated position management and debt rebalancing can run continuously without eroding yield. This architecture shifts leveraged farming away from mutualized platform risk into discrete, predictable execution. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to review the execution logs.

reddit.hook: How Vanna isolates Blend b-token margin on Soroban without shared pool contagion
reddit.copy:
Blend v2 formal verification solves math correctness for pool calculations, but it does not change the structural risk profile of shared cross-collateral lending. If you loop b-tokens in a shared pool environment, you remain exposed to systemic bad debt if an obscure collateral asset in that pool suffers an oracle failure or sudden liquidity drain.

We took a different approach when designing Vanna on Soroban. Instead of using a monolithic contract where user assets are pooled into a single balance sheet, every user spins up an isolated SmartAccount sandbox.

When you loop Blend b-tokens through Vanna, your leverage stays strictly inside your designated sandbox. The sandbox interacts directly with Blend v2 pool contracts, borrowing against collateral while keeping your risk boundary completely separated from every other user on the protocol. If another farmer gets liquidated, zero losses transfer to your position.

Execution is anchored by our Mercury indexer, delivering state validation with ~320ms latency. The contract enforces a 1.10x Health Factor floor. If market conditions deteriorate, the liquidation engine unwinds only the assets within that specific SmartAccount to cover the margin gap. Because Soroban execution costs are minimal, sitting at roughly 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per call, rebalancing bot transactions do not eat up the yields you are farming.

If you want to test the architecture or stress-test how sandboxed positions behave under simulated volatility, the testnet contracts are live.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance and inspect the contract storage keys directly in the Soroban explorer.
